content:
The test image shows a soybean leaf with numerous small, light-colored (tan/cream) raised spots/pustules scattered across the leaf surface, along with several holes where tissue has been lost. The spots appear as tiny raised bumps rather than angular, water-soaked lesions.

Key observations:
- Small, raised pustular spots across the leaf surface
- Light tan/cream coloration of the bumps
- No prominent yellow halos (rules out Bacterial Blight)
- Not gray-centered with dark borders (rules out Frogeye)
- Not dark brown irregular spots (rules out Septoria)
- The raised, blister-like nature of lesions is characteristic

This matches Bacterial Pustule: "Small light green spots with raised centers... developing light-colored pustules (blisters) in the center of lesions" with "tiny tan bumps" being a key differentiator.
